#    target's allocation and this one is all trainers. The address is
#    split out of the URL here rather than templated, because it is only
#    known at run time — it arrives through a mem:// binding.
# 2. In-allocation split (`vllm` unbound, vllm_num_servers > 0):

# 3. Off-policy (the default): every node trains.
VLLM_URL=""
VLLM_ARGS=""

  # http://host:port -> host, port. Strip the scheme, then split on the
  # LAST colon so an IPv6 literal or a missing port is not silently
  # mangled into something that fails at connect time instead of here.
  _hostport="${VLLM_URL#*://}"
  _hostport="${_hostport%%/*}"
  case "$_hostport" in
    *:*) VLLM_HOST="${_hostport%:*}"; VLLM_PORT="${_hostport##*:}" ;;
    *)   VLLM_HOST="$_hostport";      VLLM_PORT="8001" ;;
  esac
  if [ -z "$VLLM_HOST" ]; then
    echo "logit-distill: FATAL: could not parse a host out of vllm_server_url '$VLLM_URL'" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  TRAINER_NODES="$NODES"
  VLLM_ARGS="--vllm_mode server"
  VLLM_ARGS="$VLLM_ARGS --vllm_sync_frequency 1"
  VLLM_ARGS="$VLLM_ARGS --vllm_server_host $VLLM_HOST --vllm_server_port $VLLM_PORT"

    # own /etc/ld.so.cache misses libcuda.so and Triton's driver
    # discovery (which checks `ldconfig -p` before falling back to
    # LD_LIBRARY_PATH) fails with "libcuda.so cannot found!".
    # Unconditional and harmless where the gap doesn't exist (LSF,
    # or a cache that's already current) — see
    # steps/train/distill/images/gpu/README.md.
    ldconfig 2>/dev/null || true
    exec "$PYBIN" -m gb_steps_post_training.distillation.run_vllm_serve \
      --port "${KD_VLLM_API_PORT:-8001}" \
      --model "/models/student" \
      --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
      --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
      --data-parallel-size "$GPUS" \
      --log_level warning \
      --max-model-len 16384

# False sends generation down the local ZeRO-3 path

# ── Per-checkpoint artifact emission ────────────────────────────
# Rendered only when emit_checkpoint_artifacts is on, so the
# single-checkpoint recipes get byte-identical script to before.
#
# HF Trainer writes each save into ${CKPT_DIR}/checkpoint-<N>, where
# <N> is the optimizer step. A downstream export/eval target can
# start against rung N the moment it is written rather than after the
# whole run, but only if something says so mid-run — the final
# artifact at the bottom of this script is emitted once, at the end.
# So: a background loop globs the dir and emits one artifact line per
# newly completed checkpoint, which the monitor's periodic log
# retrieval scrapes while the job is still RUNNING.
#
# The emitted id is checkpoint_<N> and it MUST match the output names
# the recipe declares on this target.
CKPT_GLOB="checkpoint-"
CKPT_WATCH_INTERVAL="60"
# Completeness sentinels: a checkpoint is emitted only once ALL of
# these exist. Trainer._save_checkpoint writes in a fixed order —
# save_model (config, weights, tokenizer) -> optimizer/scheduler ->
# rng_state -> state.save_to_json(trainer_state.json) — so requiring
# the weights, the last tokenizer file AND trainer_state.json brackets
# the entire write sequence. A plain non-empty check would race it and
# hand a half-written model to an export that has already allocated.
# Sharded weights (not this 350m pair) would need
# model.safetensors.index.json here too.
CKPT_SENTINELS="model.safetensors tokenizer.json trainer_state.json"
# One marker file per emitted checkpoint. On disk rather than in a
# shell variable because emit_new_checkpoints also runs inside the
# backgrounded watcher subshell, whose variables never propagate back
# to this shell — the markers are the two halves' only shared state,
# and the final guard counts them.
EMITTED_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"


emit_new_checkpoints() {
  for ckpt in "$CKPT_DIR"/${CKPT_GLOB}*; do
    [ -d "$ckpt" ] || continue
    base="$(basename "$ckpt")"
    step="${base#${CKPT_GLOB}}"
    marker="$EMITTED_DIR/$base"
    [ -e "$marker" ] && continue
    complete=1
    for sentinel in $CKPT_SENTINELS; do
      [ -f "$ckpt/$sentinel" ] || { complete=0; break; }
    done
    [ "$complete" -eq 1 ] || continue
    touch "$marker"
    echo "GB_ARTIFACT_ID:checkpoint_${step} GB_ARTIFACT_PATH:${ckpt}"
  done
}

watch_checkpoints() {
  while true; do
    emit_new_checkpoints
    sleep "$CKPT_WATCH_INTERVAL"
  done
}

WATCH_PID=""
cleanup_watcher() {
  if [ -n "$WATCH_PID" ] && kill -0 "$WATCH_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
    kill "$WATCH_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$WATCH_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    WATCH_PID=""
  fi
}

# The trainer's commit is already recorded above as distill_code_commit,
# by the (now unconditional) source-delivery block: the trainer and the
# rest of this collection are the same baked package, so there is nothing
# left to record separately here.

# ── Resume: seed this run's checkpoint dir from an earlier run ──
# Rendered only when resume_from_checkpoint_dir is set. Runs BEFORE the
# checkpoint watcher starts, so the watcher never sees a half-linked
# directory, and before any rank reaches gold.py's checkpoint glob, so
# every rank makes the same resume-or-not decision. A split decision
# (rank 0 resumes, a worker starts fresh) would hang in the first
# collective rather than fail.
RESUME_SRC="/src/gold_node2"
RESUME_SRC="${RESUME_SRC%/}"
# rank 0 -> the other ranks: this attempt's token once the seed is done,
# "failed:<token>" if rank 0 exits first. A retry_workload relaunch reuses
# GB_BUILD_WORKDIR, so a marker already here is the previous attempt's and
# must not release anyone; the token is built as the clone handshake's is.
RESUME_SEEDED="$CKPT_DIR/.resume-seeded"
RESUME_TOKEN="${GB_SKYPILOT_LAUNCH_ID:-}:${SKYPILOT_INTERNAL_JOB_ID:-}:${LSB_JOBID:-${SLURM_JOB_ID:-}}"
# The watcher's completeness test: these bracket HF Trainer's whole save
# sequence, so a checkpoint the source run was killed while writing is
# skipped rather than resumed from. Weights are model.safetensors, or the
# index save_pretrained writes after the last shard of sharded ones.
RESUME_SENTINELS="tokenizer.json trainer_state.json"
resume_complete() {
  [ -f "$1/model.safetensors" ] || [ -f "$1/model.safetensors.index.json" ] \
    || return 1
  for sentinel in $RESUME_SENTINELS; do
    [ -f "$1/$sentinel" ] || return 1
  done
}
# ZeRO optimizer shards in a checkpoint: one per training rank. The tr
# strips the padding BSD wc adds, so the count prints the same everywhere.
resume_shards() {
  find "$1" -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 2 -path '*/global_step*/*' \
    -name '*optim_states.pt' 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]'
}
# get_last_checkpoint's name rule, ^checkpoint-[0-9]+$: HF never loads
# anything else, so nothing else is seeded, checked or picked.
resume_is_checkpoint() {
  base="${1##*/}"
  step="${base#checkpoint-}"
  [ -d "$1" ] && [ "$step" != "$base" ] && [ -n "$step" ] \
    && [ -n "${step##*[!0-9]*}" ]
}
if [ "$NODE_RANK" = "0" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$CKPT_DIR"
  # Any exit before the seed is done tells the waiting ranks at once,
  # rather than after their 900s.
  trap '[ "$(cat "$RESUME_SEEDED" 2>/dev/null || true)" = "$RESUME_TOKEN" ] \
    || { printf "failed:%s\n" "$RESUME_TOKEN" > "$RESUME_SEEDED.tmp.$$" \
    && mv -f "$RESUME_SEEDED.tmp.$$" "$RESUME_SEEDED"; } 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
  if [ ! -d "$RESUME_SRC" ]; then
    echo "logit-distill: FATAL: resume_from_checkpoint_dir '$RESUME_SRC' is not a directory." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  # An EXTERNAL server (the `vllm` input bound) is another target's allocation:
  # every node here trains, whatever vllm_num_servers says. Only the
  # in-allocation split gives nodes to vLLM -- see "Node roles" below.
  
  RESUME_WORLD=$(( (NODES - VLLM_SERVERS) * GPUS ))
  
  # What a failed attempt was writing when it died: rank 0's files missing,
  # or fewer optimizer shards than ranks (a node died mid DeepSpeed save;
  # this run's own attempts all share its topology). HF would pick it if it
  # is the highest and fail on every rank; moved aside instead, out of HF's
  # and the watcher's checkpoint-* pattern. Kept for diagnosis: the per-run
  # workdir, and these with it, is reaped when the target run tears down.
  for ckpt in "$CKPT_DIR"/checkpoint-*; do
    resume_is_checkpoint "$ckpt" || continue
    shards="$(resume_shards "$ckpt")"
    if resume_complete "$ckpt" \
      && { [ "$shards" -eq 0 ] || [ "$shards" -ge "$RESUME_WORLD" ]; }; then
      continue
    fi
    aside="$CKPT_DIR/incomplete-${ckpt##*/}.$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S)"
    mv "$ckpt" "$aside"
    echo "logit-distill: resume: moved incomplete ${ckpt##*/} aside to ${aside##*/}"
  done
  RESUME_COUNT=0
  SEED_TOP=""
  for ckpt in "$RESUME_SRC"/checkpoint-*; do
    resume_is_checkpoint "$ckpt" || continue
    if ! resume_complete "$ckpt"; then
      echo "logit-distill: resume: skipping incomplete $(basename "$ckpt")"
      continue
    fi
    if [ -e "$CKPT_DIR/$(basename "$ckpt")" ]; then
      echo "logit-distill: resume: $(basename "$ckpt") already present, not re-seeded"
    else
      cp -al "$ckpt" "$CKPT_DIR/" 2>/dev/null || cp -a "$ckpt" "$CKPT_DIR/"
      echo "logit-distill: resume: seeded $(basename "$ckpt") from $RESUME_SRC"
    fi
    RESUME_COUNT=$(( RESUME_COUNT + 1 ))
    # Numeric, not lexical: checkpoint-500 sorts after checkpoint-1500.
    step="${ckpt##*/checkpoint-}"
    if [ -z "$SEED_TOP" ] || [ "$step" -gt "$SEED_TOP" ]; then
      SEED_TOP="$step"
    fi
  done
  if [ "$RESUME_COUNT" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "logit-distill: FATAL: no complete checkpoint-* under '$RESUME_SRC'." >&2
    echo "  Resuming was asked for, so starting from step 0 instead would" >&2
    echo "  silently spend the whole schedule again." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  # Every check below is on the checkpoint the trainer resumes from:
  # gold.py calls train(resume_from_checkpoint=True), and HF's
  # get_last_checkpoint takes the highest checkpoint-<N> in CKPT_DIR. After a
  # retry that can be one the failed attempt wrote, above everything seeded.
  # Every checkpoint-<N> left here is complete.
  RESUME_CKPT=""
  for ckpt in "$CKPT_DIR"/checkpoint-*; do
    resume_is_checkpoint "$ckpt" || continue
    step="${ckpt##*/checkpoint-}"
    if [ -z "$RESUME_CKPT" ] || [ "$step" -gt "${RESUME_CKPT##*/checkpoint-}" ]; then
      RESUME_CKPT="$ckpt"
    fi
  done
  RESUME_NAME="${RESUME_CKPT##*/}"
  # A ZeRO-3 checkpoint holds one optimizer shard per rank and DeepSpeed
  # cannot load it at another world size. Checked here, on a CPU-cheap
  # count, rather than discovered by every rank after allocation.
  RESUME_SHARDS="$(resume_shards "$RESUME_CKPT")"
  if [ "$RESUME_SHARDS" -gt 0 ] && [ "$RESUME_SHARDS" -ne "$RESUME_WORLD" ]; then
    echo "logit-distill: FATAL: $RESUME_NAME holds $RESUME_SHARDS ZeRO optimizer shards" >&2
    echo "  but this run trains on $RESUME_WORLD ranks. Resume with the source's topology." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  # HF Trainer restores trainer_state.json whole on resume, and with it the
  # SOURCE run's save_steps and logging_steps: this run's --save-steps is
  # replaced with a warning nobody sees, and every rung of this run's
  # ladder that is not also on the source's grid is never written (build
  # 4c758672, A1: a 250-step ladder on c2000's 1000). Rewrite both in the
  # checkpoint the trainer resumes from. Single-quoted so an unsubstituted
  # value reaches its FATAL message instead of tripping `set -u`.
  "$PYBIN" "$DISTILL_HOME/steps/logit-distill/align_resume_state.py" --checkpoint "$RESUME_CKPT" \
    --save-steps '500' \
    --logging-steps '5'
  echo "logit-distill: resume: $RESUME_COUNT checkpoint(s) seeded; the trainer resumes from $RESUME_NAME"
  # Lineage is the seed: the source's highest complete checkpoint. A higher
  # one here was written by an earlier attempt of this run, from that seed.
  if [ "$RESUME_NAME" != "checkpoint-$SEED_TOP" ]; then
    echo "logit-distill: resume: $RESUME_NAME was written by an earlier attempt of this run, after the seed"
  fi
  echo "GB_STEP_METADATA_KEY:resumed_from GB_STEP_METADATA_VALUE:$RESUME_SRC/checkpoint-$SEED_TOP"
  printf '%s\n' "$RESUME_TOKEN" > "$RESUME_SEEDED.tmp.$$"
  mv -f "$RESUME_SEEDED.tmp.$$" "$RESUME_SEEDED"
  trap - EXIT
else
  # The checkpoint dir is on the shared filesystem, so rank 0's marker is
  # visible here once it is written. Bounded, for a rank 0 that died
  # without its EXIT trap running.
  waited=0
  while :; do
    seed="$(cat "$RESUME_SEEDED" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [ "$seed" = "$RESUME_TOKEN" ] && break
    if [ "$seed" = "failed:$RESUME_TOKEN" ]; then
      echo "logit-distill: FATAL: rank 0 failed to seed $CKPT_DIR; its log says why." >&2

    fi

      echo "logit-distill: FATAL: rank 0 did not finish seeding $CKPT_DIR within 900s." >&2
      exit 1
    fi

    waited=$(( waited + 5 ))

fi

    # Unconditional and harmless where the gap doesn't exist (LSF,
    # or a cache that's already current) — see

    ldconfig 2>/dev/null || true

# by the (now unconditional) source-delivery block: the trainer and the
# rest of this collection are the same baked package, so there is nothing
# left to record separately here.

# ── Resume: seed this run's checkpoint dir from an earlier run ──
# Rendered only when resume_from_checkpoint_dir is set. Runs BEFORE the
# checkpoint watcher starts, so the watcher never sees a half-linked
# directory, and before any rank reaches gold.py's checkpoint glob, so
# every rank makes the same resume-or-not decision. A split decision
# (rank 0 resumes, a worker starts fresh) would hang in the first
# collective rather than fail.
RESUME_SRC="/src/gold_node2"
RESUME_SRC="${RESUME_SRC%/}"
# rank 0 -> the other ranks: this attempt's token once the seed is done,
# "failed:<token>" if rank 0 exits first. A retry_workload relaunch reuses
# GB_BUILD_WORKDIR, so a marker already here is the previous attempt's and
# must not release anyone; the token is built as the clone handshake's is.
RESUME_SEEDED="$CKPT_DIR/.resume-seeded"
RESUME_TOKEN="${GB_SKYPILOT_LAUNCH_ID:-}:${SKYPILOT_INTERNAL_JOB_ID:-}:${LSB_JOBID:-${SLURM_JOB_ID:-}}"
# The watcher's completeness test: these bracket HF Trainer's whole save
# sequence, so a checkpoint the source run was killed while writing is
# skipped rather than resumed from. Weights are model.safetensors, or the
# index save_pretrained writes after the last shard of sharded ones.
RESUME_SENTINELS="tokenizer.json trainer_state.json"
resume_complete() {
  [ -f "$1/model.safetensors" ] || [ -f "$1/model.safetensors.index.json" ] \
    || return 1
  for sentinel in $RESUME_SENTINELS; do
    [ -f "$1/$sentinel" ] || return 1
  done
}
# ZeRO optimizer shards in a checkpoint: one per training rank. The tr
# strips the padding BSD wc adds, so the count prints the same everywhere.
resume_shards() {
  find "$1" -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 2 -path '*/global_step*/*' \
    -name '*optim_states.pt' 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]'
}
# get_last_checkpoint's name rule, ^checkpoint-[0-9]+$: HF never loads
# anything else, so nothing else is seeded, checked or picked.
resume_is_checkpoint() {
  base="${1##*/}"
  step="${base#checkpoint-}"
  [ -d "$1" ] && [ "$step" != "$base" ] && [ -n "$step" ] \
    && [ -n "${step##*[!0-9]*}" ]
}
if [ "$NODE_RANK" = "0" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$CKPT_DIR"
  # Any exit before the seed is done tells the waiting ranks at once,
  # rather than after their 900s.
  trap '[ "$(cat "$RESUME_SEEDED" 2>/dev/null || true)" = "$RESUME_TOKEN" ] \
    || { printf "failed:%s\n" "$RESUME_TOKEN" > "$RESUME_SEEDED.tmp.$$" \
    && mv -f "$RESUME_SEEDED.tmp.$$" "$RESUME_SEEDED"; } 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
  if [ ! -d "$RESUME_SRC" ]; then
    echo "logit-distill: FATAL: resume_from_checkpoint_dir '$RESUME_SRC' is not a directory." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  # An EXTERNAL server (the `vllm` input bound) is another target's allocation:
  # every node here trains, whatever vllm_num_servers says. Only the
  # in-allocation split gives nodes to vLLM -- see "Node roles" below.
  
  RESUME_WORLD=$(( (NODES - VLLM_SERVERS) * GPUS ))
  
  # What a failed attempt was writing when it died: rank 0's files missing,
  # or fewer optimizer shards than ranks (a node died mid DeepSpeed save;
  # this run's own attempts all share its topology). HF would pick it if it
  # is the highest and fail on every rank; moved aside instead, out of HF's
  # and the watcher's checkpoint-* pattern. Kept for diagnosis: the per-run
  # workdir, and these with it, is reaped when the target run tears down.
  for ckpt in "$CKPT_DIR"/checkpoint-*; do
    resume_is_checkpoint "$ckpt" || continue
    shards="$(resume_shards "$ckpt")"
    if resume_complete "$ckpt" \
      && { [ "$shards" -eq 0 ] || [ "$shards" -ge "$RESUME_WORLD" ]; }; then
      continue
    fi
    aside="$CKPT_DIR/incomplete-${ckpt##*/}.$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S)"
    mv "$ckpt" "$aside"
    echo "logit-distill: resume: moved incomplete ${ckpt##*/} aside to ${aside##*/}"
  done
  RESUME_COUNT=0
  SEED_TOP=""
  for ckpt in "$RESUME_SRC"/checkpoint-*; do
    resume_is_checkpoint "$ckpt" || continue
    if ! resume_complete "$ckpt"; then
      echo "logit-distill: resume: skipping incomplete $(basename "$ckpt")"
      continue
    fi
    if [ -e "$CKPT_DIR/$(basename "$ckpt")" ]; then
      echo "logit-distill: resume: $(basename "$ckpt") already present, not re-seeded"
    else
      cp -al "$ckpt" "$CKPT_DIR/" 2>/dev/null || cp -a "$ckpt" "$CKPT_DIR/"
      echo "logit-distill: resume: seeded $(basename "$ckpt") from $RESUME_SRC"
    fi
    RESUME_COUNT=$(( RESUME_COUNT + 1 ))
    # Numeric, not lexical: checkpoint-500 sorts after checkpoint-1500.
    step="${ckpt##*/checkpoint-}"
    if [ -z "$SEED_TOP" ] || [ "$step" -gt "$SEED_TOP" ]; then
      SEED_TOP="$step"
    fi
  done
  if [ "$RESUME_COUNT" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "logit-distill: FATAL: no complete checkpoint-* under '$RESUME_SRC'." >&2
    echo "  Resuming was asked for, so starting from step 0 instead would" >&2
    echo "  silently spend the whole schedule again." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  # Every check below is on the checkpoint the trainer resumes from:
  # gold.py calls train(resume_from_checkpoint=True), and HF's
  # get_last_checkpoint takes the highest checkpoint-<N> in CKPT_DIR. After a
  # retry that can be one the failed attempt wrote, above everything seeded.
  # Every checkpoint-<N> left here is complete.
  RESUME_CKPT=""
  for ckpt in "$CKPT_DIR"/checkpoint-*; do
    resume_is_checkpoint "$ckpt" || continue
    step="${ckpt##*/checkpoint-}"
    if [ -z "$RESUME_CKPT" ] || [ "$step" -gt "${RESUME_CKPT##*/checkpoint-}" ]; then
      RESUME_CKPT="$ckpt"
    fi
  done
  RESUME_NAME="${RESUME_CKPT##*/}"
  # A ZeRO-3 checkpoint holds one optimizer shard per rank and DeepSpeed
  # cannot load it at another world size. Checked here, on a CPU-cheap
  # count, rather than discovered by every rank after allocation.
  RESUME_SHARDS="$(resume_shards "$RESUME_CKPT")"
  if [ "$RESUME_SHARDS" -gt 0 ] && [ "$RESUME_SHARDS" -ne "$RESUME_WORLD" ]; then
    echo "logit-distill: FATAL: $RESUME_NAME holds $RESUME_SHARDS ZeRO optimizer shards" >&2
    echo "  but this run trains on $RESUME_WORLD ranks. Resume with the source's topology." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  # HF Trainer restores trainer_state.json whole on resume, and with it the
  # SOURCE run's save_steps and logging_steps: this run's --save-steps is
  # replaced with a warning nobody sees, and every rung of this run's
  # ladder that is not also on the source's grid is never written (build
  # 4c758672, A1: a 250-step ladder on c2000's 1000). Rewrite both in the
  # checkpoint the trainer resumes from. Single-quoted so an unsubstituted
  # value reaches its FATAL message instead of tripping `set -u`.
  "$PYBIN" "$DISTILL_HOME/steps/logit-distill/align_resume_state.py" --checkpoint "$RESUME_CKPT" \
    --save-steps '500' \
    --logging-steps '5'
  echo "logit-distill: resume: $RESUME_COUNT checkpoint(s) seeded; the trainer resumes from $RESUME_NAME"
  # Lineage is the seed: the source's highest complete checkpoint. A higher
  # one here was written by an earlier attempt of this run, from that seed.
  if [ "$RESUME_NAME" != "checkpoint-$SEED_TOP" ]; then
    echo "logit-distill: resume: $RESUME_NAME was written by an earlier attempt of this run, after the seed"
  fi
  echo "GB_STEP_METADATA_KEY:resumed_from GB_STEP_METADATA_VALUE:$RESUME_SRC/checkpoint-$SEED_TOP"
  printf '%s\n' "$RESUME_TOKEN" > "$RESUME_SEEDED.tmp.$$"
  mv -f "$RESUME_SEEDED.tmp.$$" "$RESUME_SEEDED"
  trap - EXIT
else
  # The checkpoint dir is on the shared filesystem, so rank 0's marker is
  # visible here once it is written. Bounded, for a rank 0 that died
  # without its EXIT trap running.
  waited=0
  while :; do
    seed="$(cat "$RESUME_SEEDED" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [ "$seed" = "$RESUME_TOKEN" ] && break
    if [ "$seed" = "failed:$RESUME_TOKEN" ]; then
      echo "logit-distill: FATAL: rank 0 failed to seed $CKPT_DIR; its log says why." >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$waited" -ge 900 ]; then
      echo "logit-distill: FATAL: rank 0 did not finish seeding $CKPT_DIR within 900s." >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    sleep 5
    waited=$(( waited + 5 ))
  done
  echo "logit-distill: rank $NODE_RANK: resume seed present after ${waited}s"
fi


# ── Per-checkpoint artifact emission ────────────────────────────
# Rendered only when emit_checkpoint_artifacts is on, so the
# single-checkpoint recipes get byte-identical script to before.
#
# HF Trainer writes each save into ${CKPT_DIR}/checkpoint-<N>, where
# <N> is the optimizer step. A downstream export/eval target can
# start against rung N the moment it is written rather than after the
# whole run, but only if something says so mid-run — the final
# artifact at the bottom of this script is emitted once, at the end.
# So: a background loop globs the dir and emits one artifact line per
# newly completed checkpoint, which the monitor's periodic log
# retrieval scrapes while the job is still RUNNING.
#
# The emitted id is checkpoint_<N> and it MUST match the output names
# the recipe declares on this target.
CKPT_GLOB="checkpoint-"
CKPT_WATCH_INTERVAL="60"
# Completeness sentinels: a checkpoint is emitted only once ALL of
# these exist. Trainer._save_checkpoint writes in a fixed order —
# save_model (config, weights, tokenizer) -> optimizer/scheduler ->
# rng_state -> state.save_to_json(trainer_state.json) — so requiring
# the weights, the last tokenizer file AND trainer_state.json brackets
# the entire write sequence. A plain non-empty check would race it and
# hand a half-written model to an export that has already allocated.
# Sharded weights (not this 350m pair) would need
# model.safetensors.index.json here too.
CKPT_SENTINELS="model.safetensors tokenizer.json trainer_state.json"
# One marker file per emitted checkpoint. On disk rather than in a
# shell variable because emit_new_checkpoints also runs inside the
# backgrounded watcher subshell, whose variables never propagate back
# to this shell — the markers are the two halves' only shared state,
# and the final guard counts them.
EMITTED_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"

# resume_emit_seeded is off: mark every seeded checkpoint as already
# emitted -- seeded, meaning the source holds a complete one of that name.
# After a retry_workload relaunch the dir also holds what the failed
# attempt wrote, which may never have been emitted (killed between
# watcher sweeps); those are left for the watcher.
for ckpt in "$CKPT_DIR"/${CKPT_GLOB}*; do
  [ -d "$ckpt" ] || continue
  resume_complete "$RESUME_SRC/$(basename "$ckpt")" || continue
  touch "$EMITTED_DIR/$(basename "$ckpt")"
  echo "logit-distill: resume: not re-emitting seeded $(basename "$ckpt")"
done


emit_new_checkpoints() {
  for ckpt in "$CKPT_DIR"/${CKPT_GLOB}*; do
    [ -d "$ckpt" ] || continue
    base="$(basename "$ckpt")"
    step="${base#${CKPT_GLOB}}"
    marker="$EMITTED_DIR/$base"
    [ -e "$marker" ] && continue
    complete=1
    for sentinel in $CKPT_SENTINELS; do
      [ -f "$ckpt/$sentinel" ] || { complete=0; break; }
    done
    [ "$complete" -eq 1 ] || continue
    touch "$marker"
    echo "GB_ARTIFACT_ID:checkpoint_${step} GB_ARTIFACT_PATH:${ckpt}"
  done
}

watch_checkpoints() {
  while true; do
    emit_new_checkpoints
    sleep "$CKPT_WATCH_INTERVAL"
  done
}

WATCH_PID=""
cleanup_watcher() {
  if [ -n "$WATCH_PID" ] && kill -0 "$WATCH_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
    kill "$WATCH_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$WATCH_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    WATCH_PID=""
  fi
}

# RANK 0 ONLY, for the same reason the final artifact line below is
# rank-guarded: the executor streams every node's stdout into one
# driver log, so an unguarded marker would register the same
# checkpoint N times. The watcher is started just before the trainer.
if [ "$NODE_RANK" = "0" ]; then
  # EXIT-time cleanup on every path — success, trainer failure, or
  # signal — so the loop cannot outlive the script and keep emitting.
  trap 'cleanup_watcher; rm -rf "$EMITTED_DIR"' EXIT
  mkdir -p "$CKPT_DIR"
  watch_checkpoints &
  WATCH_PID=$!
  echo "logit-distill: watching $CKPT_DIR/${CKPT_GLOB}* every ${CKPT_WATCH_INTERVAL}s (pid $WATCH_PID)"
fi

# by the (now unconditional) source-delivery block: the trainer and the

# Node roles, three cases.
#
# 1. EXTERNAL server (the `vllm` input bound): the server lives in another
#    target's allocation and this one is all trainers. The address is
#    split out of the URL here rather than templated, because it is only
#    known at run time — it arrives through a mem:// binding.
# 2. In-allocation split (`vllm` unbound, vllm_num_servers > 0):
#    the LAST N nodes serve, matching the reference launcher.
# 3. Off-policy (the default): every node trains.
VLLM_URL=""
VLLM_ARGS=""
if [ -n "$VLLM_URL" ]; then
  # http://host:port -> host, port. Strip the scheme, then split on the
  # LAST colon so an IPv6 literal or a missing port is not silently
  # mangled into something that fails at connect time instead of here.
  _hostport="${VLLM_URL#*://}"
  _hostport="${_hostport%%/*}"
  case "$_hostport" in
    *:*) VLLM_HOST="${_hostport%:*}"; VLLM_PORT="${_hostport##*:}" ;;
    *)   VLLM_HOST="$_hostport";      VLLM_PORT="8001" ;;
  esac
  if [ -z "$VLLM_HOST" ]; then
    echo "logit-distill: FATAL: could not parse a host out of vllm_server_url '$VLLM_URL'" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  TRAINER_NODES="$NODES"
  VLLM_ARGS="--vllm_mode server"
  VLLM_ARGS="$VLLM_ARGS --vllm_sync_frequency 1"
  VLLM_ARGS="$VLLM_ARGS --vllm_server_host $VLLM_HOST --vllm_server_port $VLLM_PORT"
  echo "logit-distill: external vLLM server at $VLLM_HOST:$VLLM_PORT; all $NODES node(s) train"
else
  TRAINER_NODES=$(( NODES - VLLM_SERVERS ))
  if [ "$VLLM_SERVERS" -gt 0 ] && [ "$NODE_RANK" -ge "$TRAINER_NODES" ]; then
    echo "logit-distill: rank $NODE_RANK serving the student under vLLM"
    # SLURM's pyxis/enroot builds this container in a separate srun
    # from the one that injects the NVIDIA driver, so the image's
    # own /etc/ld.so.cache misses libcuda.so and Triton's driver
    # discovery (which checks `ldconfig -p` before falling back to
    # LD_LIBRARY_PATH) fails with "libcuda.so cannot found!".

# Snapshot the rest of the node-level topology from SkyPilot's own

# is always rank 0's address — already an IP, unlike LSF's
# MASTER_ADDR, which is a short hostname needing /etc/hosts
# resolution. MASTER_PORT has no SkyPilot-generic equivalent on
# either subtype, so it's derived the same way LSF's own
# provisioner derives its port from LSB_JOBID

# GPU allocation check (ibm-granite/granite.build#604). On Slurm 25.11.x an
# --overlap job step -- SkyPilot's container keeper is one -- can be granted
# fewer of the job's GPUs than the job holds (SchedMD bug 24862, fixed in
# 26.05.3), and the container keeps the keeper's device set. Ranks past the
# visible count would then bind a GPU another rank already holds and fail
# later, far from the cause. Refuse here instead. `nvidia-smi -L` lists what
# the container's device cgroup grants and ignores CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES; a
# failed or missing nvidia-smi (0 listed) proves nothing, so only an
# undercount it reports is refused. Nothing is rewritten or worked around:
# the check holds whether the fix lands in Slurm or in SkyPilot.
GPU_WANT="${SKYPILOT_NUM_GPUS_PER_NODE:-0}"
case $GPU_WANT in ''|*[!0-9]*) GPU_WANT=0 ;; esac
GPU_SEEN="$(nvidia-smi -L 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^GPU ' || true)"

GPU_DEVS="$(ls /dev/nvidia[0-9]* 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ' || true)"
echo "logit-distill: gpu check: allocated=$GPU_WANT visible=$GPU_SEEN CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='${CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES:-<unset>}' SLURM_JOB_GPUS='${SLURM_JOB_GPUS:-}' SLURM_STEP_GPUS='${SLURM_STEP_GPUS:-}' devices='$GPU_DEVS'"
if [ "$GPU_SEEN" -ge 1 ] && [ "$GPU_SEEN" -lt "$GPU_WANT" ]; then
  echo "logit-distill: FATAL: $GPU_WANT GPU(s) were allocated (SKYPILOT_NUM_GPUS_PER_NODE) but this container can access only $GPU_SEEN (nvidia-smi -L). On SLURM this is ibm-granite/granite.build#604; rerun, or report the node." >&2

fi

   \

VLLM_SERVERS=0

# Identity derives from the ALLOCATION, never from a build parameter,
# so the checkpoint path cannot claim a node count the run did not have.
CONFIG_NAME="gold_node${NODES}"
CKPT_DIR="${GB_BUILD_WORKDIR:-$PWD}/checkpoints/${CONFIG_NAME}"
CFG="${GB_BUILD_WORKDIR:-$PWD}/gold_config_${CONFIG_NAME}.yaml"

# The trainer's commit is already recorded above as distill_code_commit,
# by the (now unconditional) source-delivery block: the trainer and the
# rest of this collection are the same baked package, so there is nothing
# left to record separately here.

# ── Resume: seed this run's checkpoint dir from an earlier run ──
# Rendered only when resume_from_checkpoint_dir is set. Runs BEFORE the
# checkpoint watcher starts, so the watcher never sees a half-linked
# directory, and before any rank reaches gold.py's checkpoint glob, so
# every rank makes the same resume-or-not decision. A split decision
# (rank 0 resumes, a worker starts fresh) would hang in the first
# collective rather than fail.
RESUME_SRC="/src/gold_node2"
RESUME_SRC="${RESUME_SRC%/}"
# rank 0 -> the other ranks: this attempt's token once the seed is done,
# "failed:<token>" if rank 0 exits first. A retry_workload relaunch reuses
# GB_BUILD_WORKDIR, so a marker already here is the previous attempt's and
# must not release anyone; the token is built as the clone handshake's is.
RESUME_SEEDED="$CKPT_DIR/.resume-seeded"
RESUME_TOKEN="${GB_SKYPILOT_LAUNCH_ID:-}:${SKYPILOT_INTERNAL_JOB_ID:-}:${LSB_JOBID:-${SLURM_JOB_ID:-}}"
# The watcher's completeness test: these bracket HF Trainer's whole save
# sequence, so a checkpoint the source run was killed while writing is
# skipped rather than resumed from. Weights are model.safetensors, or the
# index save_pretrained writes after the last shard of sharded ones.
RESUME_SENTINELS="tokenizer.json trainer_state.json"
resume_complete() {
  [ -f "$1/model.safetensors" ] || [ -f "$1/model.safetensors.index.json" ] \
    || return 1
  for sentinel in $RESUME_SENTINELS; do
    [ -f "$1/$sentinel" ] || return 1
  done
}
# ZeRO optimizer shards in a checkpoint: one per training rank. The tr
# strips the padding BSD wc adds, so the count prints the same everywhere.
resume_shards() {
  find "$1" -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 2 -path '*/global_step*/*' \
    -name '*optim_states.pt' 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]'
}
# get_last_checkpoint's name rule, ^checkpoint-[0-9]+$: HF never loads
# anything else, so nothing else is seeded, checked or picked.
resume_is_checkpoint() {
  base="${1##*/}"
  step="${base#checkpoint-}"
  [ -d "$1" ] && [ "$step" != "$base" ] && [ -n "$step" ] \
    && [ -n "${step##*[!0-9]*}" ]
}
if [ "$NODE_RANK" = "0" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$CKPT_DIR"
  # Any exit before the seed is done tells the waiting ranks at once,
  # rather than after their 900s.
  trap '[ "$(cat "$RESUME_SEEDED" 2>/dev/null || true)" = "$RESUME_TOKEN" ] \
    || { printf "failed:%s\n" "$RESUME_TOKEN" > "$RESUME_SEEDED.tmp.$$" \
    && mv -f "$RESUME_SEEDED.tmp.$$" "$RESUME_SEEDED"; } 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
  if [ ! -d "$RESUME_SRC" ]; then
    echo "logit-distill: FATAL: resume_from_checkpoint_dir '$RESUME_SRC' is not a directory." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  # An EXTERNAL server (the `vllm` input bound) is another target's allocation:
  # every node here trains, whatever vllm_num_servers says. Only the
  # in-allocation split gives nodes to vLLM -- see "Node roles" below.
  
  RESUME_WORLD=$(( NODES * GPUS ))
  
  # What a failed attempt was writing when it died: rank 0's files missing,
  # or fewer optimizer shards than ranks (a node died mid DeepSpeed save;
  # this run's own attempts all share its topology). HF would pick it if it
  # is the highest and fail on every rank; moved aside instead, out of HF's
  # and the watcher's checkpoint-* pattern. Kept for diagnosis: the per-run
  # workdir, and these with it, is reaped when the target run tears down.
  for ckpt in "$CKPT_DIR"/checkpoint-*; do
    resume_is_checkpoint "$ckpt" || continue
    shards="$(resume_shards "$ckpt")"
    if resume_complete "$ckpt" \
      && { [ "$shards" -eq 0 ] || [ "$shards" -ge "$RESUME_WORLD" ]; }; then
      continue
    fi
    aside="$CKPT_DIR/incomplete-${ckpt##*/}.$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S)"
    mv "$ckpt" "$aside"
    echo "logit-distill: resume: moved incomplete ${ckpt##*/} aside to ${aside##*/}"
  done
  RESUME_COUNT=0
  SEED_TOP=""
  for ckpt in "$RESUME_SRC"/checkpoint-*; do
    resume_is_checkpoint "$ckpt" || continue
    if ! resume_complete "$ckpt"; then
      echo "logit-distill: resume: skipping incomplete $(basename "$ckpt")"
      continue
    fi
    if [ -e "$CKPT_DIR/$(basename "$ckpt")" ]; then
      echo "logit-distill: resume: $(basename "$ckpt") already present, not re-seeded"
    else
      cp -al "$ckpt" "$CKPT_DIR/" 2>/dev/null || cp -a "$ckpt" "$CKPT_DIR/"
      echo "logit-distill: resume: seeded $(basename "$ckpt") from $RESUME_SRC"
    fi
    RESUME_COUNT=$(( RESUME_COUNT + 1 ))
    # Numeric, not lexical: checkpoint-500 sorts after checkpoint-1500.
    step="${ckpt##*/checkpoint-}"
    if [ -z "$SEED_TOP" ] || [ "$step" -gt "$SEED_TOP" ]; then
      SEED_TOP="$step"
    fi
  done
  if [ "$RESUME_COUNT" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "logit-distill: FATAL: no complete checkpoint-* under '$RESUME_SRC'." >&2
    echo "  Resuming was asked for, so starting from step 0 instead would" >&2
    echo "  silently spend the whole schedule again." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  # Every check below is on the checkpoint the trainer resumes from:
  # gold.py calls train(resume_from_checkpoint=True), and HF's
  # get_last_checkpoint takes the highest checkpoint-<N> in CKPT_DIR. After a
  # retry that can be one the failed attempt wrote, above everything seeded.
  # Every checkpoint-<N> left here is complete.
  RESUME_CKPT=""
  for ckpt in "$CKPT_DIR"/checkpoint-*; do
    resume_is_checkpoint "$ckpt" || continue
    step="${ckpt##*/checkpoint-}"
    if [ -z "$RESUME_CKPT" ] || [ "$step" -gt "${RESUME_CKPT##*/checkpoint-}" ]; then
      RESUME_CKPT="$ckpt"
    fi
  done
  RESUME_NAME="${RESUME_CKPT##*/}"
  # A ZeRO-3 checkpoint holds one optimizer shard per rank and DeepSpeed
  # cannot load it at another world size. Checked here, on a CPU-cheap
  # count, rather than discovered by every rank after allocation.
  RESUME_SHARDS="$(resume_shards "$RESUME_CKPT")"
  if [ "$RESUME_SHARDS" -gt 0 ] && [ "$RESUME_SHARDS" -ne "$RESUME_WORLD" ]; then
    echo "logit-distill: FATAL: $RESUME_NAME holds $RESUME_SHARDS ZeRO optimizer shards" >&2
    echo "  but this run trains on $RESUME_WORLD ranks. Resume with the source's topology." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  # HF Trainer restores trainer_state.json whole on resume, and with it the
  # SOURCE run's save_steps and logging_steps: this run's --save-steps is
  # replaced with a warning nobody sees, and every rung of this run's
  # ladder that is not also on the source's grid is never written (build
  # 4c758672, A1: a 250-step ladder on c2000's 1000). Rewrite both in the
  # checkpoint the trainer resumes from. Single-quoted so an unsubstituted
  # value reaches its FATAL message instead of tripping `set -u`.
  "$PYBIN" "$DISTILL_HOME/steps/logit-distill/align_resume_state.py" --checkpoint "$RESUME_CKPT" \
    --save-steps '500' \
    --logging-steps '5'
  echo "logit-distill: resume: $RESUME_COUNT checkpoint(s) seeded; the trainer resumes from $RESUME_NAME"
  # Lineage is the seed: the source's highest complete checkpoint. A higher
  # one here was written by an earlier attempt of this run, from that seed.
  if [ "$RESUME_NAME" != "checkpoint-$SEED_TOP" ]; then
    echo "logit-distill: resume: $RESUME_NAME was written by an earlier attempt of this run, after the seed"
  fi
  echo "GB_STEP_METADATA_KEY:resumed_from GB_STEP_METADATA_VALUE:$RESUME_SRC/checkpoint-$SEED_TOP"
  printf '%s\n' "$RESUME_TOKEN" > "$RESUME_SEEDED.tmp.$$"
  mv -f "$RESUME_SEEDED.tmp.$$" "$RESUME_SEEDED"
  trap - EXIT
else
  # The checkpoint dir is on the shared filesystem, so rank 0's marker is
  # visible here once it is written. Bounded, for a rank 0 that died
  # without its EXIT trap running.
  waited=0
  while :; do
    seed="$(cat "$RESUME_SEEDED" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [ "$seed" = "$RESUME_TOKEN" ] && break
    if [ "$seed" = "failed:$RESUME_TOKEN" ]; then
      echo "logit-distill: FATAL: rank 0 failed to seed $CKPT_DIR; its log says why." >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$waited" -ge 900 ]; then
      echo "logit-distill: FATAL: rank 0 did not finish seeding $CKPT_DIR within 900s." >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    sleep 5
    waited=$(( waited + 5 ))
  done
  echo "logit-distill: rank $NODE_RANK: resume seed present after ${waited}s"
fi


# ── Per-checkpoint artifact emission ────────────────────────────
# Rendered only when emit_checkpoint_artifacts is on, so the
# single-checkpoint recipes get byte-identical script to before.
#
# HF Trainer writes each save into ${CKPT_DIR}/checkpoint-<N>, where
# <N> is the optimizer step. A downstream export/eval target can
# start against rung N the moment it is written rather than after the
# whole run, but only if something says so mid-run — the final
# artifact at the bottom of this script is emitted once, at the end.
# So: a background loop globs the dir and emits one artifact line per
# newly completed checkpoint, which the monitor's periodic log
# retrieval scrapes while the job is still RUNNING.
#
# The emitted id is checkpoint_<N> and it MUST match the output names
# the recipe declares on this target.
CKPT_GLOB="checkpoint-"
CKPT_WATCH_INTERVAL="60"
# Completeness sentinels: a checkpoint is emitted only once ALL of
# these exist. Trainer._save_checkpoint writes in a fixed order —
# save_model (config, weights, tokenizer) -> optimizer/scheduler ->
# rng_state -> state.save_to_json(trainer_state.json) — so requiring
# the weights, the last tokenizer file AND trainer_state.json brackets
# the entire write sequence. A plain non-empty check would race it and
# hand a half-written model to an export that has already allocated.
# Sharded weights (not this 350m pair) would need
# model.safetensors.index.json here too.
CKPT_SENTINELS="model.safetensors tokenizer.json trainer_state.json"
# One marker file per emitted checkpoint. On disk rather than in a
# shell variable because emit_new_checkpoints also runs inside the
# backgrounded watcher subshell, whose variables never propagate back
# to this shell — the markers are the two halves' only shared state,
# and the final guard counts them.
EMITTED_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"


emit_new_checkpoints() {
  for ckpt in "$CKPT_DIR"/${CKPT_GLOB}*; do
    [ -d "$ckpt" ] || continue
    base="$(basename "$ckpt")"
    step="${base#${CKPT_GLOB}}"
    marker="$EMITTED_DIR/$base"
    [ -e "$marker" ] && continue
    complete=1
    for sentinel in $CKPT_SENTINELS; do
      [ -f "$ckpt/$sentinel" ] || { complete=0; break; }
    done
    [ "$complete" -eq 1 ] || continue
    touch "$marker"
    echo "GB_ARTIFACT_ID:checkpoint_${step} GB_ARTIFACT_PATH:${ckpt}"
  done
}

watch_checkpoints() {
  while true; do
    emit_new_checkpoints
    sleep "$CKPT_WATCH_INTERVAL"
  done
}

WATCH_PID=""
cleanup_watcher() {
  if [ -n "$WATCH_PID" ] && kill -0 "$WATCH_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
    kill "$WATCH_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$WATCH_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    WATCH_PID=""
  fi
}

# RANK 0 ONLY, for the same reason the final artifact line below is
# rank-guarded: the executor streams every node's stdout into one
# driver log, so an unguarded marker would register the same
# checkpoint N times. The watcher is started just before the trainer.
if [ "$NODE_RANK" = "0" ]; then
  # EXIT-time cleanup on every path — success, trainer failure, or
  # signal — so the loop cannot outlive the script and keep emitting.
  trap 'cleanup_watcher; rm -rf "$EMITTED_DIR"' EXIT
  mkdir -p "$CKPT_DIR"
  watch_checkpoints &
  WATCH_PID=$!
  echo "logit-distill: watching $CKPT_DIR/${CKPT_GLOB}* every ${CKPT_WATCH_INTERVAL}s (pid $WATCH_PID)"
fi


# The trainer's commit is already recorded above as distill_code_commit,
# by the (now unconditional) source-delivery block: the trainer and the

# Node roles, three cases.
#
# 1. EXTERNAL server (the `vllm` input bound): the server lives in another
#    target's allocation and this one is all trainers. The address is
#    split out of the URL here rather than templated, because it is only
#    known at run time — it arrives through a mem:// binding.
# 2. In-allocation split (`vllm` unbound, vllm_num_servers > 0):
#    the LAST N nodes serve, matching the reference launcher.
# 3. Off-policy (the default): every node trains.
VLLM_URL="http://10.0.0.1:8001"
VLLM_ARGS=""
if [ -n "$VLLM_URL" ]; then
  # http://host:port -> host, port. Strip the scheme, then split on the
  # LAST colon so an IPv6 literal or a missing port is not silently
  # mangled into something that fails at connect time instead of here.
  _hostport="${VLLM_URL#*://}"
  _hostport="${_hostport%%/*}"
  case "$_hostport" in
    *:*) VLLM_HOST="${_hostport%:*}"; VLLM_PORT="${_hostport##*:}" ;;
    *)   VLLM_HOST="$_hostport";      VLLM_PORT="8001" ;;
  esac
  if [ -z "$VLLM_HOST" ]; then
    echo "logit-distill: FATAL: could not parse a host out of vllm_server_url '$VLLM_URL'" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  TRAINER_NODES="$NODES"
  VLLM_ARGS="--vllm_mode server"
  VLLM_ARGS="$VLLM_ARGS --vllm_sync_frequency 1"
  VLLM_ARGS="$VLLM_ARGS --vllm_server_host $VLLM_HOST --vllm_server_port $VLLM_PORT"
  echo "logit-distill: external vLLM server at $VLLM_HOST:$VLLM_PORT; all $NODES node(s) train"
else
  TRAINER_NODES=$(( NODES - VLLM_SERVERS ))
  if [ "$VLLM_SERVERS" -gt 0 ] && [ "$NODE_RANK" -ge "$TRAINER_NODES" ]; then
    echo "logit-distill: rank $NODE_RANK serving the student under vLLM"
    # SLURM's pyxis/enroot builds this container in a separate srun
    # from the one that injects the NVIDIA driver, so the image's
    # own /etc/ld.so.cache misses libcuda.so and Triton's driver
    # discovery (which checks `ldconfig -p` before falling back to
    # LD_LIBRARY_PATH) fails with "libcuda.so cannot found!".
    # Unconditional and harmless where the gap doesn't exist (LSF,
    # or a cache that's already current) — see
    # steps/train/distill/images/gpu/README.md.
    ldconfig 2>/dev/null || true
    exec "$PYBIN" -m gb_steps_post_training.distillation.run_vllm_serve \
      --port "${KD_VLLM_API_PORT:-8001}" \
      --model "/models/student" \
      --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
      --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
      --data-parallel-size "$GPUS" \
      --log_level warning \
      --max-model-len 16384
  fi
fi

# --use_vllm is stated in BOTH directions below, from the same
# vllm_num_servers that gates every other on-policy key. gold.py
# defaults it to False and custom_gold_trainer.py:2003 branches on it:
# False sends generation down the local ZeRO-3 path
# (generate_on_policy_outputs) rather than to the server. Emitted only
# negatively — as it was until now — an on-policy run allocates a vLLM
# node, health-checks it, plumbs its address in, then generates locally
# and leaves the server idle. Build d77546a9 did exactly that, logged
# not one request against the server, and died in the local path.
echo "logit-distill: rank $NODE_RANK/$NODES training ($TRAINER_NODES trainer node(s)), master $MADDR:$MPORT"
accelerate launch \
  --num_processes $(( TRAINER_NODES * GPUS )) \
  --num_machines "$TRAINER_NODES" \
  --machine_rank "$NODE_RANK" \
  --main_process_ip "$MIP" \
  --main_process_port "$MPORT" \
  --config_file "$CODE_DIR/configs/deepspeed/accelerate_deepspeed_zero3.yaml" \
  -m gb_steps_post_training.distillation.gold \
  --config "$CFG" \
  --output_dir "$CKPT_DIR" \
  --use_vllm=False \
  $VLLM_ARGS


# The trainer has exited. Stop the watcher, then sweep once more for
# anything written between its last poll and that exit — including the
# final checkpoint, which on a run bounded by an epoch rather than by
# save_steps is written at a step no save grid names.
if [ "$NODE_RANK" = "0" ]; then
  cleanup_watcher
  emit_new_checkpoints

  # Fail LOUDLY on zero, because the alternative failure is silent:
  # a recipe's checkpoint_<N> outputs would never be produced, every
  # export/eval target bound to them would stay unready, and the build
  # would hang with no error to read. Count the markers, not a shell
  # variable — see EMITTED_DIR above.
  EMITTED_COUNT="$(find "$EMITTED_DIR" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type f 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]')"
  if [ "$EMITTED_COUNT" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "logit-distill: FATAL: no checkpoint dirs matched '${CKPT_DIR}/${CKPT_GLOB}*'." >&2
    echo "  emit_checkpoint_artifacts is on, so a recipe is bound to" >&2
    echo "  checkpoint_<N> ids that will now never arrive. Either the run" >&2
    echo "  never reached save_steps, or the trainer's checkpoint dir" >&2
    echo "  naming changed — align CKPT_GLOB and the recipe's ladder." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "logit-distill: emitted $EMITTED_COUNT per-checkpoint artifact(s)"
fi


# Rank 0 only: the executor streams every node's output into one
# driver log, so an unguarded marker would register N artifacts.
if [ "$NODE_RANK" = "0" ]; then
  echo "GB_ARTIFACT_ID:checkpoint GB_ARTIFACT_PATH:${CKPT_DIR}"
fi
